rawContent:
Tweet by @AnatoliKopadze (Anatoli Kopadze)
Author bio: Adapt or die
Text: This is actually f*cking gold.

I found one place where every top AI tool and every frontier model are set up to work together.

You don't pick between Claude, GPT and Grok anymore. They're all in one chat, ready to run any task you throw at it.

Writing a bot, building a CRM, cutting an ad video, spinning up UGC content, it just does the whole thing.

It's called Higgsfield Supercomputer, and the way it works comes down to six layers. Here's each one.

-------

Layer 1 - Intent

You stop writing prompts and start handing over outcomes.

"Build a working app." "Pull this research together." "Spin up a landing page and the ads for it."

A normal chat asks what to type. This layer asks what you want done, then figures out the steps on its own.

-------

Layer 2 - Routing

You don't pick the model anymore.

It runs the best ones under the hood, Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, and routes each task to whichever fits.

The best model changes almost every week. Here you stop betting your workflow on a single provider and let the system choose.

-------

Layer 3 - Free thinking

The planning is free.

Plans, research and drafts run in Free mode at zero cost, and you only spend when it renders the real output.

That means you can test ten directions before committing a cent, which quietly changes how much you're willing to explore.

-------

Layer 4 - Memory

It doesn't reset every session.

It holds your context and your style, so "make another like the last one, but for the new product" just works.

Context is the thing every chatbot keeps losing. This layer is where consistency comes from.

-------

Layer 5 - Tools

It acts inside the stack you already use.

Slack, Drive, Notion, Gmail, Figma are wired in, so the work lands where you actually work instead of a blank box.

-------

Layer 6 - Autonomy

This is the part a chat physically can't do.

You put a job on Scheduled Tasks and it runs on its own, planning and executing while you sleep.

Give it a goal once and it becomes a loop: plan, do, repeat, without you sitting in the middle.

-------

That's the whole thing - six layers, one chat and most of the work just gets done for you.

You spend less time typing questions and more time handing off outcomes.

A lot of people are still working inside the chatbox, and this feels like a step past it.

Maybe the model was never the whole story. the system around it might matter just as much.
